title: A fossil sample

doesNotKnow: The panels show 6 hard-part records but only 1 soft-part record from equally sized starting groups. This illustrates preservation bias; the toy numbers are not measured fossil rates.

misconception: The first apparent interpretation is the only possible one.
objective: In a toy sample, 10 animals have hard parts and 10 have only soft parts. If 6 hard parts and 1 soft part are preserved, which kind dominates the sample?

claims.text: In a toy sample, 10 animals have hard parts and 10 have only soft parts. If 6 hard parts and 1 soft part are preserved, which kind dominates the sample? The panels show 6 hard-part records but only 1 soft-part record from equally sized starting groups. This illustrates preservation bias; the toy numbers are not measured fossil rates. Hard: 6 of 10. Soft: 1 of 10

claims.text: The diagram is an illustrative schematic, not an observation of an actual site.
If 4 shells and 1 soft body survive from equal starting groups, which kind dominates the preserved sample? Four shells outnumber one soft-body record.
